description: Relocating the Native Village of Shishmaref, Alaska Due to Coastal Erosion is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); USACE Alaska District; Shishmaref Erosion and Relocation Coalition. The Native Village of Shishmaref is located on Sarichef Island in the Chukchi Sea. This barrier island is highly vulnerable to coastal erosion, thawing permafrost, and flooding. Relocation efforts have been underway since 2001, however, a lack of funding has delayed the process and people and infrastructure remain at risk. Coverage: Shishmaref, AK (2002). The toolkit gives Shishmaref, AK as the location, 2002 as the year and 17 years as the duration. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
